B. Only pi (nucleotide diversity) is biased.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: C. Both Watterson's estimator and pi are biased downward by the filter-then-reference-impute step.

The imputation rule is reference-biased: a true derived allele can only be turned into reference when its call is filtered, a true reference can never be turned into derived. After filtering every missing genotype is written as 0, so on every haplotype E[O_ij | G_ij=1]=1-f and E[O_ij|G_ij=0]=0 with f>0 the per-haplotype deletion probability. Hence the observed derived allele frequency at a site is attenuated on average to p_obs = p(1-f) and

E[ pairwise differences at the site ] = 2p(1-f)[1-p(1-f)] < 2p(1-p).

Averaged over the union of SNV positions that enter the VCF this is a systematic downward shift of the mean pairwise difference, so pi is biased downward for any finite f>0 and the bias does not disappear with more samples.

The same reference imputation also erodes the segregating-site count that enters Watterson's theta_W = S / a_n. A site is scored segregating in the final sequences only if at least one carrier retains a non-reference call after filtering. Conditional on k_s true derived copies in the sample the site is seen as monomorphic after imputation with probability f^{k_s}>0. For common variants k_s is large and f^{k_s} is tiny, but the segregating-site spectrum is dominated by rare variants with k_s = O(1). Under the infinite-sites model the number of such rare sites grows with n and f^{k_s} is non-negligible for them. The stated guarantee “no completely missing SNVs across all samples’’ is pre-filtering; post-filter + reference imputation a site can become invariant in the constructed sequences when all its carriers happen to be among the per-sample minority that is deleted.

Hence E[S_obs] = Σ_s [1 - f^{k_s}] < Σ_s 1 = S_true strictly for any f>0, and the inequality persists even as n is made arbitrarily large because the rare-allele tail is replenished as n grows. In expectation S is under-counted and theta_W = S/a_n is downward biased alongside pi. The bias is the classic presence/absence vs frequency distinction: reference imputation can only create false reference homozygotes, so both the frequency-weighted summary pi and the site-count summary used by Watterson are pulled toward zero.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: C. Both Watterson's estimator and pi are biased downward by the filter-and-reference-impute step.

The per-sample deletion is random and genotype independent with per-haplotype loss probability m>0. After imputation a true derived chromosome is recorded as derived with probability 1−m and as reference with probability m. Hence for a site with true haplotype frequency p
E[p̂]=p(1−m) < p
and the expected per-site heterozygosity is
E[2p̂(1−p̂)]=2p(1−m)[1−p(1−m)]<2p(1−p).
That is a frequency attenuation that is present for every site that remains in the alignment and it does not disappear with n. Pairwise differences are therefore systematically under-counted, so π is downward biased.

The same attenuation creates a threshold loss of segregating sites. A truly segregating site is observed as segregating after imputation iff at least one of its true derived copies survives filtering in its carrier. Conditional on kₛ true derived copies in the 2n haplotypes,
Pr[ site is seen as segregating | kₛ ] = 1 − m^{kₛ}.
With the VCF union used for the analysis the panel of sites is not fixed: the condition “no completely missing SNV across all samples” is pre-filtering, and with an arbitrarily large sample the union acquires ever rarer variants. Under the infinite-sites model the number of sites with kₛ =1,2,… grows with n, so the set of sites examined is itself growing.

For a fixed p>0, m^{kₛ}→0 as n→∞, but the sites that matter for the limit are not fixed-p sites. The marginal sites that are continually discovered as n grows have kₛ=O(1). For kₛ=1 the loss probability is m>0, for kₛ=2 it is m²>0, etc. The expected number of lost singletons is m·E[number of true singletons] and that expectation grows with n. In other words the limit is not uniform over the frequency spectrum: the proportion of the segregating-site count contributed by the ultra-rare tail stays non-zero, and those sites are lost with positive probability.

Hence
E[S_obs] = Σₛ [1−m^{kₛ}] < Σₛ 1 = S_true,
with strict inequality as soon as m>0. The missing genotypes are forced to the reference allele, so no new segregating sites are created, but truly segregating sites can be rendered monomorphic reference when all their carriers are filtered in that sample. Because S_obs is stochastically smaller than S_true,
E[θ_W^{obs}] = E[S_obs]/a_n < S_true/a_n = θ_W^{true}
in any finite sample and the bias does not vanish when the panel itself grows with the sample. The bias is most severe for the rare variants that dominate S, and the reference imputation enriches the alignment with false reference homozygotes.

Thus reference-biased imputation depresses both the frequency-weighted pairwise differences that define π and the presence/absence count S that defines Watterson’s θ. The “presence vs frequency” distinction holds only for a fixed set of sites with p bounded away from zero; with an arbitrarily large sample the ascertained SNV panel brings in a growing ultra-rare tail for which the loss probability m^{kₛ} remains >0. Both summaries are pulled toward zero.

C. Both Watterson’s θW and π are downward biased by the filter-and-reference-impute step.

The per-haplotype filtering is genotype independent with per-site retention probability 1−m>0, and every missing call is forced to reference. That is a systematic false negative for derived alleles. On a truly segregating site with true derived haplotype frequency p>0 the observed frequency after imputation is in expectation p_obs = p(1−m) < p, and a true pairwise difference is scored only when both copies are retained. Hence

E[π_obs(site)] = 2 p(1−m)[1−p(1−m)] < 2p(1−p),

and the inequality holds sitewise for every 0<p<1. The attenuation factor 1−m does not disappear with sample size; π is frequency weighted and is permanently pulled toward the reference.

The same reference imputation also deflates the segregating-site count S that enters θW = S/a_n. A site is observed as segregating only if at least one true derived copy survives filtering in the sample. Conditional on i true derived copies in 2n haplotypes

P[site is seen as segregating | i] = 1− m^{i}.

Under the infinite-sites coalescent the expected number of sites with i copies is θ/i. Hence

E[S_obs] = Σ_i θ/i [1− m^{i}] = θ a_{2n−1} − θ Σ_i m^{i}/i
         = θ a_{2n−1} − θ [−ln(1−m)].

Σ_i m^{i}/i = −ln(1−m) >0 is finite and independent of n. The loss term is O(1) in absolute numbers but it is dominated by the rare-variant tail: for i=1 the loss probability is m>0, for i=2 it is m², etc. Because E[#singletons]≈θ, E[#doubletons]≈θ/2, … the expected number of segregating sites that are completely masked by reference imputation is θ∑ m^{i}/i >0 for any m>0. 

The “no completely missing SNV across all samples” condition applies to the original VCF before per-sample filtering. After independent per-sample deletion a truly segregating site can become monomorphic reference in the imputed alignment whenever all its carriers in the sample happen to be filtered at that site. That happens with probability >0 for every site, and for the ultra-rare tail with i=O(1) the probability stays bounded away from zero even as n→∞ because the site frequency spectrum continually replenishes rare variants as n grows. In any realistic finite, though arbitrarily large, sample the expected observed S_obs < S_true, so θW = S_obs/a_n is downward biased as well.

Reference imputation therefore creates excess apparent reference homozygotes. It depresses pairwise differences and π through allele-frequency attenuation, and it depresses S and θW through complete masking of rare derived copies. Both summaries are biased downward.

I’m leaning toward C, both estimators being downward biased in the set-up as described.

The reference imputation is systematic, not random missingness. A true derived allele that is filtered in a haplotype is forced to 0 in the final sequence, so the observed derived count at a site is a thinned version of the true count. That thinning both lowers allele frequencies and can erase segregation at a site.

For π the point is clear: the observed pairwise difference at a site is a function of the observed frequency p_obs = p_true*(1-f) in expectation, with f>0 the per-haplotype filter rate. So E[π_obs] = 2 p_obs(1-p_obs) < 2 p_true(1-p_true) for every segregating site and the average over the panel is strictly downward biased, and that attenuation does not disappear with more samples.

The same mechanism hits S and therefore θ_W. A site is counted as segregating in the imputed alignment only if at least one true derived copy survives filtering in at least one haplotype. With independent per-sample deletion the probability a truly segregating site is seen as monomorphic reference is f^{k_s} where k_s is the number of true derived copies in the sample. That probability is >0 for any finite sample, and it is non-negligible for the rare tail that dominates the infinite-sites spectrum.

Yes, for any fixed p_s>0, f^{k_s}→0 as n→∞, but the panel that we are actually analysing is the union of SNVs that ever appear in the VCFs. Under the standard spectrum the number of sites with k_s = O(1) grows with n, in particular the expected number of singletons grows linearly with n. The expected absolute loss E[S_loss]= Σ_s f^{k_s} therefore stays positive and in practice a substantial minority of rare derived copies are turned into reference by the per-sample filter. That is the finite-sample, practical reading of “arbitrarily large”.

Hence in any realistic, finite though large, data set E[S_obs] < S_true and θ_W = S_obs/a_n is stochastically smaller than the true value on the ascertained panel. The bias of θ_W vanishes only in the mathematical limit n→∞, while the bias of π persists even in that limit. Because the question is about the calculation we actually perform on the imputed sequences, both the segregating-site count and the frequency-weighted pairwise differences are deflated by the reference-biased imputation.

That matches the intuition that reference imputation creates an excess of false reference homozygotes, depressing both the site-frequency spectrum used by π and the count of polymorphic sites used by Watterson’s θ.

C. Both Watterson's theta and pi are biased downward by the filter-and-impute procedure.

The imputation rule is Oij = Gij if the call is kept and Oij = reference otherwise. A true derived allele can only be turned into reference, never the reverse, and the per-haplotype loss probability f>0 is independent of genotype. That gives in expectation

E[ p̂_obs | p_true ] = p_true (1-f) < p_true

for every truly segregating site. The observed pairwise difference at the site is therefore

E[ 2 p̂_obs (1-p̂_obs) ] = 2 p_true (1-f) [1 - p_true (1-f)] < 2 p_true (1-p_true)

so the site heterozygosity and the genome-wide average pairwise difference π are systematically attenuated. The attenuation is a constant factor in allele frequency and does not disappear with n.

The same reference-biased imputation also deflates the segregating site count that enters Watterson’s estimator. A site is scored as segregating only if at least one derived copy survives filtering in the panel. Conditional on k_s true derived copies in the 2n haplotypes,

Pr[site appears monomorphic after imputation | k_s] = f^{k_s} >0

and

E[S_obs] = Σ_s [1 - f^{k_s}] < Σ_s 1 = S_true

for any f>0. The loss probability is non-negligible for the rare tail that dominates S under the infinite sites model. Even with an arbitrarily large sample, the site frequency spectrum contains variants with k_s = O(1) when p_true ~ 1/n, and f^{k_s} is bounded away from zero for those variants. The condition that no SNV is completely absent from the union of VCFs only guarantees ascertainment of the sites, not that every copy of the derived allele is retained in every carrier. Because deletion is sample-specific and random, low-frequency derived alleles are regularly masked in all carriers in a realized data set and are subsequently imputed to reference homozygotes, so the observed S_obs is stochastically smaller than S_true in expectation.

Hence θ_W = S_obs / a_n is downward biased together with π, with π additionally suffering the frequency attenuation  p → p(1-f). The segregation vs frequency distinction is correct in the strict n→∞ limit for fixed p>0, but with a realistic, albeit arbitrarily large, sample the rare variant contribution keeps E[S_obs] < S_true and both summaries are pulled toward the reference by the non-random imputation.

C. Both Watterson's estimator and pi are biased downward by the filter-then-reference-impute step.

The imputation rule is reference-biased: a true derived allele can only be turned into reference when its call is filtered, a true reference can never be turned into derived. After filtering every missing genotype is written as 0, so on every haplotype E[O_ij | G_ij=1]=1-f and E[O_ij|G_ij=0]=0 with f>0 the per-haplotype deletion probability. Hence the observed derived allele frequency at a site is attenuated on average to p_obs = p(1-f) and

E[ pairwise differences at the site ] = 2p(1-f)[1-p(1-f)] < 2p(1-p).

Averaged over the union of SNV positions that enter the VCF this is a systematic downward shift of the mean pairwise difference, so pi is biased downward for any finite f>0 and the bias does not disappear with more samples.

The same reference imputation also erodes the segregating-site count that enters Watterson's theta_W = S / a_n. A site is scored segregating in the final sequences only if at least one carrier retains a non-reference call after filtering. Conditional on k_s true derived copies in the sample the site is seen as monomorphic after imputation with probability f^{k_s}>0. For common variants k_s is large and f^{k_s} is tiny, but the segregating-site spectrum is dominated by rare variants with k_s = O(1). Under the infinite-sites model the number of such rare sites grows with n and f^{k_s} is non-negligible for them. The stated guarantee “no completely missing SNVs across all samples’’ is pre-filtering; post-filter + reference imputation a site can become invariant in the constructed sequences when all its carriers happen to be among the per-sample minority that is deleted.

Hence E[S_obs] = Σ_s [1 - f^{k_s}] < Σ_s 1 = S_true strictly for any f>0, and the inequality persists even as n is made arbitrarily large because the rare-allele tail is replenished as n grows. In expectation S is under-counted and theta_W = S/a_n is downward biased alongside pi. The bias is the classic presence/absence vs frequency distinction: reference imputation can only create false reference homozygotes, so both the frequency-weighted summary pi and the site-count summary used by Watterson are pulled toward zero.

Pr[ site is seen as segregating | kₛ ] = 1 − m^{kₛ}.

E[S_obs] = Σₛ [1−m^{kₛ}] < Σₛ 1 = S_true,
with strict inequality as soon as m>0. constant frequency scaling produced by turning every filtered derived
copy into reference.  It does not vanish with $n$ and
$E[\pi_{obs}]<\pi_{true}$ for every $f>0$.  No false derived alleles can
be created, so pairwise differences are permanently deflated.

Segregation is presence/absence.  Conditional on $k_{s}=2np_{s}$ true
derived copies

$\Pr\{{\rm site\;s\;lost\;after\;imputation}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{\,k_{s}}$

i.e. the site is seen as monomorphic reference iff all $k_{s}$ carriers are
filtered in their own samples.  With the stated ascertainment the panel
${\cal L}$ is the union of truly segregating SNVs, $p_{s}>0\;\forall s\in{\cal L}$,
and retained calls are accurate so no false segregating sites are created.

For any fixed $p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}\to\infty$ with $n$ and $f^{k_{s}}\to0$.  Hence

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s\in{\cal L}}\!\left[1-f^{k_{s}}\right]
\longrightarrow\sum_{s\in{\cal L}}1=S_{true}$ ,

$S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}$ and

$\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}/a_{n}
=\theta_{W}^{true}$

on the ascertained SNV panel.  The absolute loss
$\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}=\theta\sum_{i}f^{i}/i=-\theta\ln(1-f)=O(1)$
is the classic $k_{s}=O(1)$ rare-tail loss.  Relative to
$a_{n}\sim\log n$ it is $o(1)$ and vanishes in the $n\to\infty$ limit
stated in the problem.  

Thus the presence/absence statistic underlying Watterson’s $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$
is asymptotically recovered whereas the frequency weighted statistic
$\pi$ remains permanently attenuated by the $1-f$ reference bias.  In any
finite $n$ $E[S_{obs}]<S_{true}$ and both summaries are downward biased in
practice, which is the usual finite-sample $C$ caveat.  In the arbitrarily
large-sample limit required here the bias that survives is the frequency
bias of $\pi$ only.

B. Only $\pi$ is biased in the $n\to\infty$ limit; Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$
is asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained SNV panel.

11.text:
With a per-haplotype, genotype independent deletion probability f>0 and
deterministic reference imputation

Oij = Gij with prob. 1-f,  Oij = 0 with prob. f  if Gij=1,
Oij = 0 a.s. if Gij=0

retained calls are correct.  For a true derived haplotype frequency p>0

E[ p̂obs | p ] = p(1-f) < p                              

in every haplotype. Hence on a site

E[ Hobs ] = 2 p̂obs (1-p̂obs) = 2p(1-f)[1-p(1-f)] < 2p(1-p)=Htrue

and

πobs = L-1 Σs 2p̂sobs(1-p̂sobs)

is stochastically smaller than the true pairwise difference. The
1-f attenuation of the observed derived frequency is a constant
frequency bias. It does not disappear with n. Reference imputation can
only turn derived → reference, it can never create a derived allele, so
the frequency weighted mean pairwise difference is permanently pulled
towards the reference. E[πobs] < πtrue for every f>0 and the bias
persists as n→∞.

Segregation is presence/absence. Let ks=2np s be the true number of
derived copies at site s. Conditional on ks

Pr{ site s is seen as monomorphic after imputation | ks } = f^{ks}

and

E[Sobs]= Σs [1-f^{ks}] .

For any fixed p s>0, ks→∞ with n and f^{ks}→0. With the stated
ascertainment that no SNV is completely absent from the union of the
VCFs the panel is the true SNV panel p s>0 ∀ s and no false segregating
sites are created by imputation. Hence

Pr{ Sobs = Strue } → 1 ,   n→∞

and on the ascertained SNV panel

θWobs = Sobs / a n →p Strue / a n = θWtrue

up to the common SNV ascertainment.  The absolute loss Σs f^{ks} is
O(1)=θ Σi f^{i}/i = θ[-ln(1-f)] and its relative contribution to
S/a n ∼ log n vanishes. In the n→∞ limit the chance that every true
copy of a p>0 site is simultaneously filtered vanishes, so the
segregating-site count, and therefore Watterson’s θW = S/a n, is
asymptotically recovered.

The usual finite-n caveat is that E[Sobs] < Strue for any fixed n
because f^{ks}>0 for the k s = O(1) rare tail, so in any realistic
finite though large sample both S and π are downward biased.  In the
strict arbitrarily large sample limit stated in the problem the
presence/absence statistic is asymptotically unbiased whereas the
frequency weighted statistic remains permanently attenuated by the
1-f reference imputation.

That is the classic segregation vs frequency sensitivity: π is
permanently biased downward, θW is asymptotically unbiased on the
ascertained SNV panel.  B. Only π is biased in the arbitrarily large
sample limit; the finite-sample version of the argument is the C both
biased statement.

6.text:
Per-haplotype genotype independent thinning with retention probability
$q=1-f>0$ followed by deterministic reference imputation is

$O_{ih}=G_{ih}{\bf1}\{{\rm kept}\},\qquad 
E[O_{ih}\mid G_{ih}=1]=q,\;E[O_{ih}\mid G_{ih}=0]=0 $

so on a true derived haplotype frequency $p_{s}>0$

$E[\hat p_{s}^{obs}\mid p_{s}]=q\,p_{s}<p_{s}$.

In particular

$E[H_{s}^{obs}]=2\hat p_{s}^{obs}\!\left[1-\hat p_{s}^{obs}\right]
      =2q p_{s}\!\left[1-q p_{s}\right]<2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=H_{s}^{true}$

sitewise for every $0<p_{s}<1$ and $0<f<1$.  
Hence

$\pi_{obs}=L^{-1}\sum_{s}2\hat p_{s}^{obs}(1-\hat p_{s}^{obs})$

is a frequency weighted statistic whose expectation is permanently
attenuated by the $q$ factor.  With the LLN for a fixed site
$\hat p_{s}^{obs}\to q p_{s}$ a.s. and

$\pi_{s}^{obs}\to2q p_{s}\!\left[1-q p_{s}\right]<2p_{s}(1-p_{s})$,

so $E[\pi_{obs}]<\pi_{true}$ for every $f>0$ and the attenuation does not
vanish with $n$.  Reference imputation can only turn derived→reference;
pairwise differences are therefore systematically deflated.

Segregation is presence/absence.  Let $k_{s}=2np_{s}$ be the true number of
derived copies at $s$.  Conditional on $k_{s}$ the site is seen as
monomorphic after imputation iff all $k_{s}$ copies are filtered,

$\Pr\{{\rm lost}_{s}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{\,k_{s}}$,

and

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s}\big[\,1-f^{\,k_{s}}\big]$.

For any fixed $p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}\to\infty$ with $n$ and
$f^{k_{s}}\to0$.  With the VCF ascertainment that the union panel is the
true SNV panel, $p_{s}>0\;\forall s$, and no false segregating sites are
created by reference imputation,

$S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true},\qquad
\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}/a_{n}
=\theta_{W}^{true}$

on the ascertained panel.  The absolute loss
$\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}= \theta\sum_{i\ge1}f^{i}/i=-\theta\ln(1-f)=O(1)$
is dominated by the $k_{s}=O(1)$ tail and its relative contribution to
$S/a_{n}\sim\log n$ vanishes.  Hence in the $n\to\infty$ limit stated in the
problem the presence/absence information underlying Watterson’s
$\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is recovered asymptotically, whereas the frequency
information underlying $\pi$ remains permanently attenuated by the $1-f$
reference imputation.

In any finite $n$ $E[S_{obs}]<S_{true}$ and both summaries are
downward biased in absolute terms, the Watterson bias being
$O\big(a_{n}^{-1}\big)\to0$.  In the arbitrarily large sample limit the
only systematic bias that survives is that of nucleotide diversity.

B. Only pi is biased in the stated large-$n$ limit; Watterson’s
$\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained SNV panel.

For any fixed $p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}\to\infty$ with $n$ and $f^{k_{s}}\to0$.

relative contribution to $S/a_{n}\sim\log n$ is $O(a_{n}^{-1})\to0$.

3.text:
With genotype independent per-haplotype deletion followed by deterministic
reference imputation a true derived chromosome is recorded as derived with
probability $1-f$ and as reference with probability $f$, $0<f<1$, and a true
reference chromosome is never turned into derived.  Retained calls are
accurate.

Let $p_{s}>0$ be the true haplotype frequency of a biallelic SNV on the
ascertained union panel and $k_{s}=2np_{s}$ the number of true derived
copies in the $2n$ phased haplotypes.  Then

$E[\hat p_{s}\mid p_{s}]=(1-f)p_{s}<p_{s}$,

so that on the site

$E[H_{s}^{\rm obs}]=2\hat p_{s}\big[1-\hat p_{s}\big]
   =2(1-f)p_{s}\Big[1-(1-f)p_{s}\Big]<2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=H_{s}^{true}$

for every $0<p_{s}<1$.  Hence

$\pi_{obs}=L^{-1}\sum_{s}2\hat p_{s}\big[1-\hat p_{s}\big]
   \to L^{-1}\sum_{s}2(1-f)p_{s}\big[1-(1-f)p_{s}\big]<\pi_{true}$

and the $1-f$ frequency attenuation is a permanent frequency bias.  Pairwise
differences are frequency weighted and the reference imputation which can
only turn derived$\to$reference systematically depresses them.  The bias
does not vanish with $n$.

Presence/absence is different.  Conditional on $k_{s}$ the site is seen as
monomorphic after imputation iff all $k_{s}$ true copies are filtered,

$\Pr\{{\rm lost}_{s}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{\,k_{s}},\qquad 
E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s}\big[1-f^{\,k_{s}}\big].$

No false segregating sites are created by reference imputation.
For any fixed $p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}=2np_{s}\to\infty$ with $n$ and
$f^{\,k_{s}}\to0$.  With the stated ascertainment that every SNV is present
in at least one sample before filtering, $\Pr\{S_{obs}=S_{true}\}\to1$ and

$S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}/a_{n}$,

so that on the ascertained SNV panel

$\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{p}
\theta_{W}^{\rm true}$

up to the common SNV ascertainment.  The absolute loss
$\sum_{s}f^{\,k_{s}}=\theta[-{\rm ln}(1-f)]+o(1)$ is $O(1)$ whereas
$a_{n}\sim\log n\to\infty$, i.e. the relative loss of $S$ is $O(1/a_{n})\to0$.
In the $n\to\infty$ limit the chance that every carrier of a $p_{s}>0$ site
is simultaneously filtered vanishes, so segregation is asymptotically
recovered whereas the frequency based $\pi$ remains attenuated by the
constant $1-f$ factor.

In any finite $n$ the $k_{s}=O(1)$ tail gives a small finite-sample
downward bias $E[S_{obs}]<S_{true}$, the usual finite-sample version of the
statement, but in the arbitrarily large sample limit stated for the
calculation the only systematic bias that survives is the frequency bias of
nucleotide diversity.  This is the classic segregation versus frequency
sensitivity of $S$ versus $\pi$.

B. Only $\pi$ is biased in the arbitrarily large sample limit; Watterson’s
$\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained SNV panel.
In a strictly finite sample both statistics are downward biased, with $\pi$
permanently attenuated and $\theta_{W}$ only $O(1/a_{n})$ downward biased.

Reference imputation is reference biased. A true derived copy is kept with probability $1-m>0$ and is written as reference with probability $m$, a true reference can never be turned into derived. Hence on a site with true haplotype frequency $p>0$ $E[\hat p_{obs}\mid p]=(1-m)p

0$, $k_{s}\to\infty$ with $n$ and $m^{k_{s}}\to0$. With the stated ascertainment $p_{s}>0$ on the union panel of SNVs and retained calls being accurate, no false segregating sites are created. Hence on the ascertained SNV set $S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true},\qquad \theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}/a_{n} =\theta_{W}^{true},\qquad n\to\infty,$ i.e. the $O(1)$ loss $\sum_{s}m^{k_{s}}$ is $o(a_{n})$ and its relative contribution to $S/a_{n}\sim\log n$ vanishes. The probability that every carrier of a $p_{s}>0$ site is simultaneously filtered goes to zero, so presence/absence is asymptotically recovered whereas the frequency weighted pairwise difference remains permanently attenuated by the $1-m$ factor. In any finite $n$ there is the familiar $O(1/a_{n})$ finite-sample downward loss $E[S_{obs}]

12.text:
The filtering + reference imputation is genotype independent on the derived
allele and it can only turn derived → reference.

Write $f\in(0,1)$ for the per-haplotype per-site filter probability and
$G_{is}\in\{0,1\}$ for the true derived indicator.  On the final alignment

$O_{is}=G_{is}$ with prob. $1-f$, $O_{is}=0$ with prob. $f$ if $G_{is}=1$,
$O_{is}=0$ a.s. if $G_{is}=0$,

so that for a site with true haplotype frequency $p_{s}>0$

$E[\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs}\mid p_{s}]=(1-f)p_{s}<p_{s}$

and, with the usual LLN for a fixed $s$,

$\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs}\xrightarrow{a.s.}(1-f)p_{s}$.

Hence

$H_{s}^{\rm obs}=2\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs}(1-\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs})
\rightarrow 2(1-f)p_{s}\bigl[1-(1-f)p_{s}\bigr]
<2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=H_{s}^{\rm true}$

for every $0<p_{s}<1$.  Averaging over the ascertained SNV panel

$\pi_{\rm obs}=L^{-1}\sum_{s}2\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs}(1-\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs})$

is therefore frequency weighted and is permanently pulled toward the
reference by the $p\mapsto (1-f)p$ attenuation.  The bias does not vanish
with $n$,

$E[\pi_{\rm obs}] <\pi_{\rm true}\qquad\forall f>0$,

and it is a systematic downward bias of nucleotide diversity.

Segregation is presence/absence.  Let $k_{s}=2np_{s}$ be the true number of
derived copies in the $2n$ haplotypes.  The site is seen as monomorphic
after imputation iff all $k_{s}$ copies are filtered,

$\Pr\{{\rm lost}_{s}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{\,k_{s}},\qquad 
E[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{s}\bigl[1-f^{\,k_{s}}\bigr]$.

For any fixed $p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}\to\infty$ with $n$ and $f^{k_{s}}\to0$.
The panel is the union of SNVs present before filtering, so
$p_{s}>0\;\forall s$ and no false segregating sites are created by
reference imputation, which can only create reference homozygotes.  Hence

$S_{\rm obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{\rm true},\qquad 
\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}
S_{\rm true}/a_{n}=\theta_{W}^{\rm true}$

on the ascertained SNV set.  In the infinite-sites limit

$E[S_{\rm obs}]=\theta\sum_{i=1}^{2n-1}\frac{1-f^{i}}{i}
 =\theta a_{2n-1}-\theta\sum_{i\ge1}\frac{f^{i}}{i}
 =\theta a_{2n-1}-\theta[-\ln(1-f)]$,

so the absolute loss is the $O(1)$ term $\theta[-\ln(1-f)]$ while
$a_{n}\sim\log n\to\infty$.  The relative bias of $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$
hence vanishes as $n\to\infty$; the presence/absence statistic is
asymptotically recovered whereas the frequency weighted statistic $\pi$
remains attenuated by the constant $1-f$ factor.

In any finite $n$ $E[S_{\rm obs}]<S_{\rm true}$ and both summaries are
downward biased in practice, the usual $O(1/a_{n})$ finite-sample loss of
the $k_{s}=O(1)$ tail.  In the arbitrarily large-sample limit stated in
the problem the surviving systematic bias is the frequency bias of
$\pi$; Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased for the
ascertained SNV panel.

That is the B position.

C. Both Watterson’s θW and π are downward biased by filter-then-reference-impute.

The imputation rule is reference-biased: a true derived allele is recorded as derived only when its call is kept, otherwise it is written as reference. With per-haplotype loss probability m>0 and genotype-independent filtering

E[ ˆp | p ] = p(1-m) < p

and for every truly segregating site

E[2 ˆp(1- ˆp)] = 2p(1-m)[1-p(1-m)] < 2p(1-p).

That is a permanent frequency attenuation. The pairwise difference that defines π is therefore systematically deflated and the attenuation does not vanish with n. This is the frequency-weighted bias.

The same operation also erodes the segregating-site count. Conditional on k_s true derived copies in the 2n haplotypes a site is seen as segregating after imputation iff at least one copy survives filtering,

Pr[site seen | k_s] = 1 - m^{k_s}.

Hence

E[S_obs] = Σ_s [1 - m^{k_s}] < Σ_s 1 = S_true

for any m>0. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is pre-filtering; after independent per-sample deletion a truly segregating site can become monomorphic reference in the constructed alignment whenever all its carriers in the sample happen to be filtered at that site.

Pointwise f^{k_s}→0 for any fixed p_s>0, but Watterson’s S is a sum over the whole ascertained frequency spectrum and the panel itself grows with n. Under infinite sites the expected number of sites with k derived copies is ≈θ/k, so the expected absolute loss is

E[S_true - S_obs] ≈ Σ_{k≥1} θ/k m^{k} = θ[-ln(1-m)] >0,

independent of n. The loss is driven by the ultra-rare tail k=O(1): for singletons loss probability is m>0, for doubletons m²>0, etc. As n increases the ascertained SNV union continually replenishes sites with p_s = O(1/n), so k_s stays O(1) for a non-vanishing fraction of the panel. The limit n→∞ does not commute with the sum over sites.

Reference imputation therefore creates excess apparent reference homozygotes. It depresses allele frequencies and π through the 1-m factor, and it depresses S and θW= S/a_n through complete masking of rare derived copies. Both summaries are pulled toward zero, with π additionally suffering the frequency attenuation p→p(1-m). The finite-sample downward bias in S that colleagues 4,6,8 already concede is the manifestation of this systematic loss of the rare tail.

The filter–then–reference-impute step is genotype independent thinning
followed by a deterministic reference fill-in.  Let $f\in(0,1)$ be the
per-haplotype per-site deletion probability and let $G_{ih}\in\{0,1\}$ be
the true derived indicator.  With retained calls accurate

$O_{ih}=G_{ih}{\bf1}\{\hbox{kept}\}$ ,  $E[O_{ih}\mid G_{ih}=1]=1-f$ ,
$E[O_{ih}\mid G_{ih}=0]=0 $

so that for a site with true haplotype frequency $p_{s}>0$

$E[\hat p_{s}^{obs}\mid p_{s}]=(1-f)p_{s}<p_{s}$ .

Hence

$E[H_{s}^{obs}]=2\hat p_{s}^{obs}\bigl[1-\hat p_{s}^{obs}\bigr]
 =2(1-f)p_{s}\bigl[1-(1-f)p_{s}\bigr]<2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=H_{s}^{true}$

site-wise for every $0<p_{s}<1$, and

$\pi_{obs}=L^{-1}\sum_{s}2\hat p_{s}^{obs}\bigl[1-\hat p_{s}^{obs}\bigr]$

is a frequency weighted statistic.  The $p\mapsto(1-f)p$ attenuation is a
constant frequency scaling produced by turning every filtered derived
copy into reference.  It does not vanish with $n$ and
$E[\pi_{obs}]<\pi_{true}$ for every $f>0$.  No false derived alleles can
be created, so pairwise differences are permanently deflated.

Segregation is presence/absence.  Conditional on $k_{s}=2np_{s}$ true
derived copies

$\Pr\{{\rm site\;s\;lost\;after\;imputation}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{\,k_{s}}$

i.e. the site is seen as monomorphic reference iff all $k_{s}$ carriers are
filtered in their own samples.  With the stated ascertainment the panel
${\cal L}$ is the union of truly segregating SNVs, $p_{s}>0\;\forall s\in{\cal L}$,
and retained calls are accurate so no false segregating sites are created.

For any fixed $p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}\to\infty$ with $n$ and $f^{k_{s}}\to0$.  Hence

$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s\in{\cal L}}\!\left[1-f^{k_{s}}\right]
\longrightarrow\sum_{s\in{\cal L}}1=S_{true}$ ,

$S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}$ and

$\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}/a_{n}
=\theta_{W}^{true}$

on the ascertained SNV panel.  The absolute loss
$\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}=\theta\sum_{i}f^{i}/i=-\theta\ln(1-f)=O(1)$
is the classic $k_{s}=O(1)$ rare-tail loss.  Relative to
$a_{n}\sim\log n$ it is $o(1)$ and vanishes in the $n\to\infty$ limit
stated in the problem.  

Thus the presence/absence statistic underlying Watterson’s $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$
is asymptotically recovered whereas the frequency weighted statistic
$\pi$ remains permanently attenuated by the $1-f$ reference bias.  In any
finite $n$ $E[S_{obs}]<S_{true}$ and both summaries are downward biased in
practice, which is the usual finite-sample $C$ caveat.  In the arbitrarily
large-sample limit required here the bias that survives is the frequency
bias of $\pi$ only.

B. Only $\pi$ is biased in the $n\to\infty$ limit; Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$
is asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained SNV panel.

\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}/a_{n}=\theta_{W}^{true}$

on the ascertained panel.  The absolute loss $\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}
=\theta\sum_{i}f^{i}/i=-\theta\ln(1-f)=O(1)$ is $o(a_{n})$ with
$a_{n}\sim\log n$, so the relative bias of $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ vanishes in
the $n\to\infty$ per-site limit.  In particular
$\Pr\{S_{obs}=S_{true}\}\to1$ for every $p_{s}>0$ site.

Hence in the arbitrarily large-sample limit that is formulated the
presence/absence statistic underlying Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$ is
asymptotically recovered on the ascertained SNV panel whereas the
frequency-weighted statistic $\pi$ remains permanently attenuated by the
$1-f$ reference bias.  The finite-$n$ version of the same argument is
$E[S_{obs}]<S_{true}$ with $E[S_{true}-S_{obs}]
=\theta[-\ln(1-f)]>0$, i.e. the usual $O(1/a_{n})$ downward loss from the
$k_{s}=O(1)$ rare tail, which is the source of the practical “both biased’’
statement $C$.

8.text:
Reference imputation is reference biased.  Let $f\in(0,1)$ be the per haplotype per site
filter probability and let a retained call be correct.  On the final
alignment

$O_{ih}=G_{ih}$ w.p. $1-f$, $O_{ih}=0$ w.p. $f$ if $G_{ih}=1$, 
$O_{ih}=0$ a.s. if $G_{ih}=0$,

so that for a site with true derived haplotype frequency $p_{s}>0$

$E[\hat p_{s}^{obs}\mid p_{s}]=(1-f)p_{s}<p_{s}$,

and with the LLN for a fixed site $\hat p_{s}^{obs}\to(1-f)p_{s}$ a.s.

Hence

$H_{s}^{obs}=2\hat p_{s}^{obs}(1-\hat p_{s}^{obs})\to
2(1-f)p_{s}\bigl[1-(1-f)p_{s}\bigr]<2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=H_{s}^{true}$

sitewise for every $0<p_{s}<1$.  The $p\mapsto(1-f)p$ attenuation is a
constant frequency shrinkage produced by turning every filtered derived
copy into reference. It cannot be removed by increasing $n$ and

$\pi_{obs}=L^{-1}\sum_{s}2\hat p_{s}^{obs}(1-\hat p_{s}^{obs})$

is a frequency weighted mean pairwise difference.  Reference imputation can
only turn derived $\to$ reference, never the reverse, so

$E[\pi_{obs}]<\pi_{true}\qquad\forall f>0$,

and the downward bias persists as $n\to\infty$.

Segregation is presence/absence.  With $k_{s}=2np_{s}$ true derived copies

$\Pr\{{\rm site\;s\;lost\;after\;imputation}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{k_{s}},\qquad
E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s}[1-f^{k_{s}}]$.

Retained calls are accurate so no false segregating sites are created.
The panel ${\cal L}$ is the union of SNVs that ever appear before filtering,
$p_{s}>0\;\forall s\in{\cal L}$, and the stated ascertainment is
pre-filter.  For any fixed $p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}\to\infty$ with $n$ and
$f^{k_{s}}\to0$.  Hence

$S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true},\qquad
\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}/a_{n}
=\theta_{W}^{true}$

on the ascertained SNV panel.  In the infinite-sites limit

$E[S_{obs}]=\theta a_{2n-1}-\theta\sum_{i\ge1}f^{i}/i
          =\theta a_{2n-1}-\theta[-\ln(1-f)]$,

so the absolute loss $\theta[-\ln(1-f)]$ is $O(1)$ whereas
$a_{n}\sim\log n\to\infty$.  The relative bias of
$\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is $O(1/a_{n})\to0$.  The $O(1)$ loss is the
$k_{s}=O(1)$ rare tail, $E[S_{true}-S_{obs}]\approx\sum_{i}\theta/i f^{i}$,
which is the familiar finite-$n$ downward bias of $S$.  It is a
$O(a_{n}^{-1})$ effect for Watterson’s estimator and vanishes in the
$n\to\infty$ limit stated in the problem.

Hence in the arbitrarily large sample limit the presence/absence statistic
underlying $S$ and $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is asymptotically recovered
whereas the frequency weighted statistic $\pi$ remains permanently
attenuated by the constant $1-f$ reference bias.  In any strictly finite,
though arbitrarily large, sample $E[S_{obs}]<S_{true}$ and both summaries
are absolutely downward biased, the $O(1/a_{n})$ finite-sample version of the
C statement.  For the $n\to\infty$ limit formulated in the question the
surviving systematic bias is that of nucleotide diversity only.

That is the segregation vs frequency sensitivity: $B$ in the
arbitrarily large-sample limit, with the finite-sample $C$ caveat noted
above.

12.text:
Reference imputation is a reference-biased thinning.  Write $f\in(0,1)$ for the
per-haplotype per-site deletion probability and $q=1-f$ for retention.
Retained calls are accurate so on the final alignment

$O_{ih}=G_{ih}$ w.p. $q$, $O_{ih}=0$ w.p. $f$ if $G_{ih}=1$,
$O_{ih}=0$ a.s. if $G_{ih}=0$,

so for a site with true derived haplotype frequency $p_{s}>0$

$E[\hat p_{s}^{obs}\mid p_{s}]=q\,p_{s}<p_{s}$,

and with the LLN for a fixed $s$

$\hat p_{s}^{obs}\xrightarrow{a.s.}q\,p_{s}$.

Hence sitewise

$H_{s}^{obs}=2\hat p_{s}^{obs}\!\left[1-\hat p_{s}^{obs}\right]
 \to2q p_{s}\!\left[1-q p_{s}\right]
 <2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=H_{s}^{true} $

for every $0<p_{s}<1$.  Nucleotide diversity is frequency weighted

$\pi_{\rm obs}=L^{-1}\sum_{s}2\hat p_{s}^{obs}(1-\hat p_{s}^{obs})
 \to L^{-1}\sum_{s}2q p_{s}(1-q p_{s})<\pi_{\rm true},$

i.e. $p\mapsto q p$ is a constant frequency shrinkage.  Reference
imputation can only turn derived$\to$reference, never the reverse, so
pairwise differences are permanently deflated. $E[\pi_{\rm obs}]<\pi_{\rm
true}$ for every $f>0$ and the $q$ attenuation does not vanish with $n$.

Segregation is presence/absence.  Let $k_{s}=2n p_{s}$ be the true number of
derived copies.  Conditional on $k_{s}$

$\Pr\{{\rm site\;s\;lost}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{\,k_{s}},\qquad
E[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{s}\!\left[1-f^{\,k_{s}}\right].$

No false segregating sites are created by reference imputation and with the
stated ascertainment the panel ${\cal L}$ is the true SNV panel,
$p_{s}>0\;\forall s\in{\cal L}$.  For any fixed $p_{s}>0$,
$k_{s}\to\infty$ with $n$ and $f^{k_{s}}\to0$.  Hence

$S_{\rm obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{\rm true},\qquad
\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}=S_{\rm obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}
S_{\rm true}/a_{n}=\theta_{W}^{\rm true}$

on the ascertained SNV set.  In the infinite-sites limit

$E[S_{\rm obs}]=\theta a_{2n-1}-\theta\sum_{i\ge1}f^{i}/i
 =\theta a_{2n-1}-\theta[-\ln(1-f)],$

so the absolute loss $\sum_{s}f^{k_{s}}=\theta[-\ln(1-f)]=O(1)$ is the
$k_{s}=O(1)$ rare-tail loss.  Relative to $a_{n}\sim\log n$ it is
$o(1)$ and

$E[\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}]=\theta_{W}^{\rm true}\!\left[1-O\!\left(a_{n}^{-1}\right)\right]
\to\theta_{W}^{\rm true}.$

The chance that every carrier of a $p_{s}>0$ site is simultaneously
filtered vanishes as $n\to\infty$.  Presence/absence is therefore
asymptotically recovered whereas the frequency weighted statistic $\pi$
remains permanently attenuated by the $1-f$ reference bias.  In any finite
$n$ $E[S_{\rm obs}]<S_{\rm true}$ and both summaries are downward biased
in absolute terms, the familiar $O(a_{n}^{-1})$ finite-sample loss of the
rare tail, but in the arbitrarily large-sample limit stated in the problem
the systematic bias that survives is the frequency bias of $\pi$ only.

B. Only $\pi$ is biased in the $n\to\infty$ limit; Watterson’s $\theta_{W}$
is asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained SNV panel, with the usual
finite-$n$ $O(1/a_{n})$ downward loss of $S$ being the source of the
finite-sample “both biased’’ remark.

I think the C reading is the one that matches the set-up as written. Reference imputation is a systematic false negative, not random missingness. With per-haplotype retention 1-f and deterministic reference fill-in we have E[p̂|p]=p(1-f)

0. The problem is that the panel we actually compute on is not a fixed set of p_s>0 sites. The VCF union condition is pre-filter. After independent per-sample deletion plus deterministic reference imputation a truly segregating site becomes invariant reference in the constructed alignment whenever all of its carriers in the sample happen to be filtered at that site. Under infinite sites the expected number of sites with i derived copies is ≈θ/i and that expectation grows with n. The expected absolute loss of segregating sites is E[S_true - S_obs] = Σ_i θ/i f^{i} = θ[-ln(1-f)] > 0, dominated by the i=O(1) tail: singletons are lost with probability f>0, doubletons with f²>0, etc. As n increases the SNV panel is continually replenished with new ultra-rare variants with p_s = O(1/n), so k_s stays O(1) forever for a non-vanishing fraction of the panel. The loss probability is bounded away from zero on exactly the sites that dominate S. Hence E[S_obs]= Σ_s[1-f^{k_s}] < S_true for any finite, though arbitrarily large, n, and the bias propagates to θ_W = S/a_n. Reference imputation therefore creates excess reference homozygotes. It depresses allele frequencies and π through the p→p(1-f) attenuation, and it depresses S and θ_W through complete masking of the rare derived copies that are constantly being added as the sample grows. In any realistic, arbitrarily large but finite sample both summaries are pulled toward the reference. Both Watterson’s θ_W and π are downward biased by the filter-then-reference-impute step.

I think the both-biased reading is the one that matches the data construction we actually perform.

Reference imputation is reference-biased. A true derived copy is kept with probability 1−f>0 and is written as reference otherwise, a true reference can never become derived. Hence for a site with true haplotype frequency p>0

E[ p̂ | p ] = p(1−f) < p

and

E[ 2p̂(1−p̂) ] = 2p(1−f)[1−p(1−f)] < 2p(1−p)

so the frequency weighted pairwise difference that defines π is
permanently pulled toward the reference by the constant 1−f attenuation.
That attenuation does not disappear with n and E[π_obs]<π_true for every f>0.

The same mechanism hits the segregating-site count. Conditional on k_s true derived copies in the 2n haplotypes a site is seen as segregating after filter+impute iff at least one copy survives filtering,

Pr[site seen | k_s] = 1 − f^{k_s}.

Hence

E[S_obs] = Σ_s [1−f^{k_s}] < Σ_s 1 = S_true,    f>0.

The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is pre-filter.
After independent per-sample deletion a truly segregating site can become monomorphic reference in the constructed alignment whenever all its carriers in the sample happen to be filtered at that site. That is a genuine false negative for segregation, not just a frequency shift.

The point-wise limit f^{k_s}→0 for fixed p_s>0 is correct, but the limit is not uniform over the spectrum we analyse. The panel we compute on is the VCF union and under infinite sites it is continually replenished with rare variants as n grows. E[#sites with i derived copies]≈θ/i, so

E[S_true−S_obs] ≈ Σ_{i≥1} θ/i f^{i}=θ[−ln(1−f)]>0,

independent of n. The loss is dominated by the ultra-rare tail k_s=O(1): singletons are lost with probability f>0, doubletons with f²>0, etc. As the sample gets larger the ascertained SNV union keeps discovering new p_s∼1/n sites, so k_s stays O(1) for a non-vanishing fraction of the panel.

Reference imputation therefore creates an excess of apparent reference homozygotes. It depresses allele frequencies and π through the p→p(1−f) attenuation, and it depresses S and θ_W=S/a_n through complete masking of the rare derived copies that dominate the infinite-sites spectrum. The absolute undercount of S is O(1) and remains positive for any finite though arbitrarily large sample; the relative O(1/a_n) loss that the B camp notes is exactly the finite-sample downward bias in Watterson’s estimator.

In the calculation we actually perform both summaries are pulled toward the reference: π by the permanent frequency shrinkage and θ_W by the systematic loss of the rare tail that is continually replenished as n grows. Both are downward biased.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the finite-sample, non-uniform aspect is what we actually compute, and it’s the reason the both-biased reading lines up with the construction as written.

Reference imputation is a systematic false negative. With per-haplotype retention q=1−f,

E[ p̂_obs | p ] = q p < p

and

E[ H_obs ] = 2 q p [1 − q p ] < 2 p (1 − p)

sitewise for every 0<p<1. Reference imputation can only turn derived → reference, never the reverse, so the frequency weighted pairwise difference that defines π is permanently attenuated by the constant q factor. That is uncontroversial and does not vanish with n.

The segregation side is the same mechanism applied to presence/absence. Conditional on k_s true derived copies

Pr{ site seen after filter+impute | k_s } = 1 − f^{k_s}

so

E[ S_obs ] = Σ_s [1 − f^{k_s}] < S_true

for any f>0. The “no completely missing SNV across all samples’’ condition is pre-filter. After independent per-sample deletion plus deterministic reference fill-in a truly segregating site becomes monomorphic reference in the built alignment whenever all of its carriers in the sample happen to be filtered at that site. Retained calls are accurate so we create no false segregating sites, only false negatives.

The point-wise limit f^{k_s}→0 for a fixed p_s>0 is correct, but it is not uniform over the spectrum we analyse. The VCF union panel is not fixed. Under infinite sites E[# sites with i copies]≈θ/i and the panel is continually replenished with ultra-rare variants as n grows. The expected absolute loss of segregating sites is

E[ S_true − S_obs ] = Σ_{i≥1} θ/i f^{i} = θ [−ln(1−f)] > 0,

independent of n, dominated by the i=O(1) tail: singletons lost with probability f>0, doubletons with f²>0, etc. As the sample is made larger the ascertainment keeps adding new p_s∼O(1/n) sites, so k_s stays O(1) for a non-vanishing fraction of the panel. The sites that dominate S are precisely those for which f^{k_s} stays bounded away from zero.

Hence for any finite, though arbitrarily large, sample

E[ S_obs ] < S_true

bias that survives is the frequency bias of nucleotide diversity. Watterson’s
$\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained SNV panel;
$\pi$ is not.

The finite-$n$ version is $E[S_{\rm obs}]<S_{\rm true}$ with
$E[S_{\rm true}-S_{\rm obs}]=\theta[-\ln(1-f)]>0$, i.e. the usual $O(a_{n}^{-1})$
downward loss of the rare tail, which is the source of the practical
both-downward statement.

12.text:
With per haplotype genotype independent loss $f>0$, $q=1-f$, and accurate
retained calls

$O_{ih}=G_{ih}\;{\rm w.p.}\;q$, $O_{ih}=0\;{\rm w.p.}\;f$ if $G_{ih}=1$,
$O_{ih}=0\;{\rm a.s.}$ if $G_{ih}=0$,

so a true derived chromosome is written derived with probability $q$ and
is written reference with probability $f$.  For a site with true derived
haplotype frequency $p_{s}>0$

$E[\hat p_{s}^{obs}\mid p_{s}]=q p_{s}<p_{s}$,

and with the LLN for a fixed $s$ $\hat p_{s}^{obs}\to q p_{s}$ a.s.  Hence

$H_{s}^{obs}=2\hat p_{s}^{obs}\!\left[1-\hat p_{s}^{obs}\right]
\to2q p_{s}\!\left[1-q p_{s}\right]
<2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=H_{s}^{true}$,

$0<p_{s}<1$, sitewise.  Reference imputation can only turn
derived$\to$reference, never the reverse, so the frequency weighted mean

$\pi_{obs}=L^{-1}\sum_{s}2\hat p_{s}^{obs}(1-\hat p_{s}^{obs})$

is permanently attenuated by the constant $p\mapsto qp$ shrinkage.
$E[\pi_{obs}]<\pi_{true}$ for every $f>0$ and the attenuation does not
vanish with $n$. Nucleotide diversity is therefore systematically pulled
toward the reference.

Segregation is presence/absence.  With $k_{s}=2np_{s}$ true derived copies

${\rm Pr}\{ {\rm site\;s\;lost\;after\;imputation}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{k_{s}}$,
$E[S_{obs}]=\sum_{s}\!\left[1-f^{k_{s}}\right]$.

No false segregating sites are created by reference imputation.  On the
ascertained VCF union panel $p_{s}>0\;\forall s$.  For any fixed
$p_{s}>0$, $k_{s}\to\infty$ with $n$ and $f^{k_{s}}\to0$, so

$S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true},\qquad 
\theta_{W}^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_{n}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}/a_{n}
=\theta_{W}^{true}$

on the ascertained SNV panel.  Under infinite sites

$E[S_{obs}]=\theta a_{2n-1}-\theta\sum_{i\ge1}f^{i}/i
 =\theta a_{2n-1}-\theta[-\ln(1-f)]$,

i.e. an $O(1)$ absolute loss $\theta[-\ln(1-f)]>0$ from the $k_{s}=O(1)$
rare tail.  Relative to $a_{n}\sim\log n$ this is $O(a_{n}^{-1})\to0$, so
the presence/absence statistic underlying Watterson’s estimator is
asymptotically recovered whereas the frequency weighted statistic $\pi$
remains permanently attenuated by the $1-f$ reference bias.  In strictly
finite $n$ $E[S_{obs}]<S_{true}$ so the usual $O(a_{n}^{-1})$ finite-sample
downward loss of $S$ and of $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$ is present, the classic
segregation versus frequency sensitivity.  In the $n\to\infty$ limit
formulated in the problem the surviving systematic bias is confined to
$\pi$.

B. Only $\pi$ is biased in the arbitrarily large-sample limit; Watterson’s
$\theta_{W}$ is asymptotically unbiased on the ascertained SNV panel, the
finite-sample $E[S_{obs}]<S_{true}$ being the $O(1/a_{n})$ rare-tail loss
that is the source of the practical both-downward biased statement.

11.text:
Reference imputation is a genotype independent thinning on the derived
allele followed by deterministic reference fill in.

For a true derived haplotype frequency p_s>0 on a fixed site

O_{ih}=G_{ih}  w.p. q=1-f ,  O_{ih}=0 w.p. f  if G_{ih}=1,
O_{ih}=0 a.s.                 if G_{ih}=0,

retained calls are accurate so no false derived alleles are created.
Hence

E[ \hat p_s^{obs} | p_s ] = q p_s < p_s ,
\hat p_s^{obs}\xrightarrow{a.s.} q p_s

and sitewise

H_s^{obs}=2\hat p_s^{obs}\!\left[1-\hat p_s^{obs}\right]
\to 2q p_s\!\left[1-qp_s\right] <2p_s(1-p_s)=H_s^{true}

for every 0<p_s<1.  Nucleotide diversity is the frequency weighted mean

\pi_{obs}=L^{-1}\sum_s H_s^{obs}\to
L^{-1}\sum_s 2q p_s[1-qp_s]<L^{-1}\sum_s 2p_s(1-p_s)=\pi_{true}.

The p\mapsto qp shrinkage is a constant frequency attenuation. Reference
imputation can only turn derived → reference, never the reverse, so
pairwise differences are permanently deflated

E[\pi_{obs}]<\pi_{true}\quad\forall f>0,

and the attenuation does not vanish with n.  That is the permanent
frequency bias of \pi.

Segregation is presence/absence.  Let k_s=2np_s be the true number of
derived copies. Conditional on k_s

Pr{site s lost after filter+impute | k_s}=f^{k_s},
Pr{site s seen segregating | k_s}=1-f^{k_s},

E[S_{obs}]=\sum_s[1-f^{k_s}].

No false segregating sites are created.  On the pre-filter ascertained
SNV panel \mathcal L=\{s:p_s>0\} we have p_s>0\;\forall s\in\mathcal L.
For any fixed p_s>0, k_s\to\infty with n and f^{k_s}\to0, so

S_{obs}\xrightarrow{p}S_{true},\qquad
\theta_W^{obs}=S_{obs}/a_n\xrightarrow{p}S_{true}/a_n=\theta_W^{true}

on the ascertained panel.  In the infinite-sites limit

E[S_{obs}]=\theta a_{2n-1}-\theta\sum_{i\ge1}f^{i}/i
          =\theta a_{2n-1}-\theta[-\ln(1-f)],

so the absolute loss \sum_s f^{k_s}= \theta[-\ln(1-f)]=O(1) is the
k_s=O(1) rare-tail loss.  Relative to a_n\sim\log n it is O(a_n^{-1})\to0.
Hence presence/absence is asymptotically recovered whereas the
frequency weighted statistic \pi remains permanently attenuated by the
1-f factor.

In any strictly finite n E[S_{obs}]<S_{true} and
E[\theta_W^{obs}]=\theta_W^{true}[1-O(a_n^{-1})]<\theta_W^{true},
the familiar O(1/a_n) finite-sample downward loss from the rare tail,
which is the source of the practical both-downward biased statement.
In the arbitrarily large-sample limit formulated in the question the
systematic bias that survives is the frequency bias of nucleotide diversity
only.  That is the classic segregation versus frequency sensitivity:
\theta_W=S/a_n is asymptotically recovered on the ascertained SNV panel,
\pi is not.

B. Only \pi is biased in the n\to\infty limit; Watterson’s \theta_W is
asymptotically unbiased for the ascertained panel, with the usual
finite-n O(a_n^{-1}) downward loss of S being the finite-sample
counterpart of the C statement.

2.text:
Reference imputation after genotype independent per haplotype thinning is a
reference biased thinning.

Write $f\in(0,1)$ for the per haplotype per site filter probability and
$q=1-f$ for retention. Retained calls are correct so on the final
alignment

$O_{ih}=G_{ih}$ w.p. $q$, $O_{ih}=0$ w.p. $f$ if $G_{ih}=1$, 
$O_{ih}=0$ a.s. if $G_{ih}=0$,

i.e. a true derived chromosome is recorded derived with probability $q$
and is written reference with probability $f$, a true reference is never
turned derived. For a site with true derived haplotype frequency $p_{s}>0$

$E[\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs}\mid p_{s}]=q\,p_{s}<p_{s}$,

and with the LLN for a fixed site $\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs}\to q p_{s}$ a.s.
Hence

$H_{s}^{\rm obs}=2\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs}\!\left[1-\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs}\right]
\to 2q p_{s}\!\left[1-q p_{s}\right]<2p_{s}(1-p_{s})=H_{s}^{\rm true}$

sitewise. Nucleotide diversity

$\pi_{\rm obs}=L^{-1}\sum_{s}2\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs}(1-\hat p_{s}^{\rm obs})$

is frequency weighted. The $p\mapsto q p$ attenuation is a constant
sitewise frequency shrinkage produced by turning every filtered derived
copy into reference. Reference imputation can only turn derived$\to$
reference, it can never create a derived allele, so pairwise differences
are permanently deflated

$E[\pi_{\rm obs}]<\pi_{\rm true}\qquad\forall f>0,$

and the $q$ factor does not vanish with $n$.

Segregation is presence/absence.  Let $k_{s}=2np_{s}$ be the true number
of derived copies. Conditional on $k_{s}$ the site is seen as segregating
after filter+impute iff at least one copy survives filtering,

$\Pr\{{\rm site\;s\;seen}\mid k_{s}\}=1-f^{k_{s}},\qquad
\Pr\{{\rm lost}\mid k_{s}\}=f^{k_{s}}>0,$

so that with the pre-filter ascertainment $p_{s}>0\;\forall s$ on the VCF
union

$E[S_{\rm obs}]=\sum_{s}\!\left[1-f^{k_{s}}\right]<\sum_{s}1=S_{\rm true}$

for any $f>0$. No false segregating sites are created by reference
imputation, only false reference homozygotes. The “no completely missing
SNV across all samples’’ condition is pre-filter. After independent
per-sample deletion a truly segregating site is scored monomorphic
reference in the constructed alignment whenever all of its $k_{s}$
carriers happen to be filtered in those samples.

Pointwise $f^{k_{s}}\to0$ for a fixed $p_{s}>0$ as $n\to\infty$, but the
panel ${\cal L}$ we compute on is the VCF union. Under infinite sites
$E[\#{\rm sites\;with\;}i{\rm \;copies}]\approx\theta/i$ and the panel is
continually replenished with $k_{s}=O(1)$ ultra rare variants as $n$
grows. The expected absolute loss of segregating sites is therefore

$E[S_{\rm true}-S_{\rm obs}]
 =\sum_{i\ge1}\frac{\theta}{i}f^{i}
 =\theta\sum_{i\ge1}f^{i}/i
 =\theta[-\ln(1-f)]>0,$

independent of $n$, dominated by the $i=O(1)$ rare tail: singletons are
lost with probability $f>0$, doubletons with $f^{2}>0$, etc. Hence for
any finite, though arbitrarily large, sample

$E[S_{\rm obs}]<S_{\rm true},\qquad
E[\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}]=E[S_{\rm obs}]/a_{n}
<\theta_{W}^{\rm true},$

with the Watterson bias $\approx-\theta[-\ln(1-f)]/a_{n}<0$, $a_{n}\sim\log n$.
The relative loss is $O(a_{n}^{-1})\to0$, the classic non-uniform
convergence, but the expectation is strictly negative for every $n$ at
which the calculation is actually performed.

Reference imputation therefore creates an excess of apparent reference
homozygotes. It depresses allele frequencies and $\pi$ through the
$p\to qp$ attenuation, and it depresses $S$ and $\theta_{W}=S/a_{n}$
through complete masking of the rare derived copies that are continually
added as the sample grows. In the operational calculation on the
imputed sequences both summaries are pulled toward the reference. In the
strict $n\to\infty$ per-site limit the relative Watterson bias vanishes
and the surviving systematic bias is the permanent frequency bias of
$\pi$, the classic segregation vs frequency sensitivity. On the finite
but arbitrarily large samples we actually compute, both Watterson’s
$\theta_{W}$ and $\pi$ are downward biased.

That is the both-downward, C, reading of the filter-then-reference-impute
step.

 =\sum_{i\ge1}\frac{\theta}{i}f^{i}
 =\theta\sum_{i\ge1}f^{i}/i
 =\theta[-\ln(1-f)]>0,$

independent of $n$, dominated by the $i=O(1)$ rare tail: singletons are

E[\theta_{W}^{\rm obs}]=E[S_{\rm obs}]/a_{n}
<\theta_{W}^{\rm true},$

added as the sample grows. In the operational calculation on the

and the surviving systematic bias is the permanent frequency bias of
$\pi$, the classic segregation vs frequency sensitivity. On the finite
but arbitrarily large samples we actually compute, both Watterson’s
$\theta_{W}$ and $\pi$ are downward biased.

step.
